title: lore check and sync spawn one quest task view per task; use one task list per run cached by the .quest tree hash
description: DEC-282 item 1, filed from ODOC-610 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T23:03Z). VERBATIM: 'lore-cli, with quest-cli for any field gap: one quest task list --json per run, never a per-task view. Missing fields are added to list's JSON (or a multi-id view) by quest-cli. Cache per run keyed by the .quest tree hash. Proof: measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, plus a test that the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count.' CONTEXT from the report: lore check and sync spawn one quest task view <id> --json per task, about 9 at a time, confirmed at src/adapters/quest.ts:456; 83 s wall per check at 574 tasks; on 2026-11-12 four to five concurrent runs made about 45 quest processes, a load of about 128, and a fleet shutdown. FIELD GAP MEASURED HERE on quest 0.14.1, 786 tasks: the lore:tasks rollup needs only id, title, status and the task file, and task list --json already carries id, title, status and path (path covers the file), so the per-task views are pure waste on this path. Fields detail() reads that list does NOT carry: subtasks, reporter and revision (all three exit 2 as unknown fields); file is covered by path. references, modifiedFiles and finalSummary ARE populated by list, checked against records that actually hold values rather than a null from a record that has none. Ships in the next lore/quest pair (DEC-282 items 1-4 ship together).

acceptanceCriteria.text: One quest task list --json per check and per sync run on the rollup path; no per-task task view spawns (measured: zero on that path).
The list read is cached per run, keyed by the .quest tree hash, and a changed tree invalidates the cache.
Measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, recording spawn count and wall time.
A test asserts the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count (N tasks, constant spawns).
Any field gap is named with the quest-cli ticket that adds it; today the rollup needs no gap, and subtasks, reporter and revision are named as the fields list lacks if a consumer needs them.

implementationNotes:
Built 2026-11-19 on branch fix/LCLI-791-one-quest-list-per-run. Rollup path (check, sync) now reads ONE quest task list per run via a new optional TrackerAdapter.taskRollup, cached across runs at .lore/cache/quest/task-list.json under sha256(quest version + every file under .quest). Zero task views on that path; lore tasks, link and orphans still view per task (unchanged); a backend without taskRollup falls back to per-task views.
Evidence: test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts (6 tests): control = per-task path costs N views; total spawns identical for 3, 30 and 300 tasks with 0 views and 1 list; gatherReconciliation rows identical; missing id gives the same not_found; second run over an unchanged tree makes 0 list calls, a changed tree re-reads; corrupt cache is a miss. Test commit predicted the pre-build state (import failure); mutant forcing the per-task fallback gives 5 red with the control green. Full bun test: 5423 pass, 3 fail, all LCLI-614 real-quest race tests (known local pair-lock artifact, CI is the judge). typecheck and biome clean.
MEASURED, real quest 0.14.1 on this repo at 794 tasks (NOT the 2000 AC3 names, and the replaced operations rather than lore end to end, because the local pair lock refuses a real lore run): 794 quest task view at 8 concurrent = 26.5 s wall and 794 spawns; one quest task list = 0.146 s and 1 spawn. AC3 therefore stays UNCHECKED pending a 2000-task measurement.
FIELD GAP: none for the rollup (id, title, status, path all in list). task list lacks subtasks, reporter and revision, which only viewTask/detail consumers (lore link, lore tasks) read; no quest-cli ticket needed today.

ROUND-2 DESIGN, as merged in #735 (e8764dfb) and refined in the follow-up PR; this SUPERSEDES the first note above where they differ. The rollup read is `quest task list --include-archived --json` (the pinned 0.14.1 accepts the flag; task view resolves archived records, so the list must). It is served through TaskRollupIndex.lookup(id): ids and aliases both resolve, a reference matching more than one record raises a conflict naming task_reference_ambiguous (as quest's findTask does) instead of picking a winner, and only the LOOKED-UP records are validated, aliases included, so an unlinked malformed record cannot fail a rollup. The cross-run cache at .lore/cache/quest/task-list.json is keyed by sha256 of the lore version, the quest version and every file under .quest (questListCacheKey), and a write re-hashes the tree and is skipped unless the key still holds, so a quest write landing during the list is never cached under the pre-write key (remaining window: an exact A-to-B-to-A revert inside one ~0.15 s list call). lore tasks, link and orphans still view per task. Tests: test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts, 23 tests, each new behaviour with a mutant that goes red. AC3 stays UNCHECKED: it needs the 2000-task end-to-end measurement against a pair-matched quest 0.15.0 including a WARM run (nothing yet proves a real-binary cache hit); the earlier 794-task figure times only the replaced operations.

Review of opum-ai/lore-cli#745. I worked read-only: no shell, and I did not run anything.
The five fixes match the findings as recorded on LCLI-791. The remaining concerns are the fold table's provenance and completeness, the breadth of the F7 throw, and a few test gaps. None is a blocker on its own, but I'd want the first two answered before APPROVE.
FINDINGS
1. MEDIUM — the fold table looks incomplete and has no drift test (src/adapters/quest.ts:~996-1016, FOLD_OVERRIDE_DATA). U+1FBE (GREEK PROSGEGRAMMENI) is absent from the data. In CaseFolding.txt it is `1FBE; C; 03B9`. Its toLowerCase() is itself, so with no override it will not fold to ι. I grepped the file for U+1FBE, U+1FD3, U+1FE3 and U+0130 and found none of them. U+0130 agrees with toLowerCase (i + U+0307), so its absence is fine. U+1FD3, U+1FE3 and U+FB05 (full foldings, or simple ones in newer Unicode versions) depend on the library's Unicode version. I could not check that. If unicode-case-folding@1.1.1 does emit 1FBE, the generator or the "294 entries" claim is wrong. If it does not, then Quest itself has the gap and lore matches Quest. Either way, "every canonical code point folds identically" (docblock) is unproven. There is no generator script in the repo. A grep for "unicode-case-folding" and FOLD_OVERRIDE finds only quest.ts and the completed LCLI-654 record. There is no drift test either. Nothing compares the table to the library, to Quest's aliasKey, or to the full CaseFolding set. Requested: commit the generator under scripts/, plus a test that pins the entry count and a hash of the data. Better, a differential test against `quest task view` or the library for every code point where fold != toLowerCase. At minimum add a U+1FBE case. Quest could change its Unicode version, and nothing here would notice.
2. MEDIUM (design point, F7) — the malformed-aliases throw is over-broad (src/adapters/quest.ts:~1067-1077). It is not too broad for correctness: a miss that might have been an alias on the unparseable record cannot honestly be not_found. It is loud, and it never spawns a view. It is too broad for blast radius. One hand-edited record with `aliases: 5` makes every lookup that misses fail with drift. That includes legitimate not_found cases such as a stale or typo'd link, and every unrelated id that has no match. In a 2000-task tracker that is a tracker-wide failure of lore check and sync from one bad record. The old behaviour was local to the matched record. The message does name the record, which helps. But the per-task path only fails for the one task asked about. Cheaper option that is still correct: scope the throw to references that could plausibly match. For a malformed string aliases value, compare referenceKey of the string itself. For a non-string, non-array value, it genuinely cannot be decided, so drift is right. Alternative: keep the throw but cap or dedupe the id list in the message. It is unbounded today (a join over every malformed id). Alternative: accept it, but record it explicitly as a decision (DEC-level) rather than a comment. Test gap: the F7 test only covers `aliases: "OLD"`. Nothing tests `aliases: ["ok", 5]` (mixed), `aliases: null` (skipped, fine) or a miss when the malformed record is irrelevant. That last one is the over-breadth case, and it needs a test pinning whichever behaviour you choose. Also check that an id with `aliases: []` plus a malformed sibling still resolves when the lookup hits (it does: matched hits skip the throw).
3. LOW — the matched path now validates aliases twice (:1079 `strings(item.aliases ?? [])`), and the index build already rejects a malformed list. That is redundant but harmless. Note that a matched record with malformed aliases is now only reachable via a collision with another record's id. Otherwise it lands in the miss branch and throws a different message. Check that no test or consumer depends on the old "matched record malformed" text. The existing `badAliases` test (T-3) probably still passes through the miss branch now, which changes the error message and not just the path. I could not confirm the pre-existing test's assertion.
4. LOW — the F1 tests rely on an implicit fixture (test: the "CALL SITE" describe). The expected key depends on the empty tree digest, i.e. on `beforeEach` leaving only the empty tasks/ directory. If any fixture ever writes a file, the tests go red for the wrong reason, or the mutant coverage silently changes. Treat the mutant claim as the writer's evidence only. I could not run it. The seeded-hit test is a good witness for both stated mutants. The tests seed the cache file with `file:` rows, not `path:`, yet the rollupItem comment says lore reads `path`. Confirm rollupItem accepts both. Otherwise the hit test passes only because the id row is found.
5. LOW — F2 and the F5 tests are sound. The self-alias test pins `held.includes`. ß/ss ambiguity, final sigma, NFC/NFD and ASCII are covered. Test coverage of the 294-entry table is about 3 entries (ß, ς, NFC). Ligatures, Cherokee and iota subscript are untested, so a transcription error in the data would go unnoticed. The data is dense literal Unicode in a string, and a decomposed-vs-composed mixup in the source file (e.g. ǰ, ΐ, ẖ lines look identical to their keys) is easy to introduce. A test that for each entry asserts the key is not the output, except the documented identity-looking ones, would catch it.
6. LOW — the F4 docblock move is correct. questListCacheKey now has its own docblock and questListCache sits under the long one. Matches the finding.
7. INFO — empty-reference behaviour differs from Quest (Quest rejects it, lore treats it as a miss). This is documented in the docblock, and with F7 an empty reference can now throw drift if any record is malformed. That is an odd interaction, but minor.
CHECK ANSWERS: (1) F1, F2, F4, F5 and F7 each have a matching change and a test. F7 is implemented more broadly than the finding asked for (finding 2 above). (2) The table is claimed to be generated from unicode-case-folding@1.1.1. I cannot see a generator, a sync test or the entry count in the repo, and U+1FBE looks missing. (3) See finding 2. (4) No regression found in the batched read path. There is still one list and no view. The cache key construction is unchanged in value, so there is no new cache miss. Exit codes follow from drift versus not_found, so the observable change is a missing id now exiting as drift when any record is malformed. (5) Test strength is adequate for F1, F2 and F5 representatives. It is thin for the table and for the F7 breadth.
COULD NOT VERIFY (no shell): whether any of the 32 tests pass, and the mutant results; whether unicode-case-folding@1.1.1 has a 1FBE entry, the actual entry count (294) or the library's Unicode version; whether Quest's aliasKey is the same as the library's output (quest-cli has no node_modules in the tree I could read); whether the old badAliases assertion still matches the new message; whether rollupItem accepts `file` in cached rows.

DISPOSITIONS OF THE OWED #737 FINDINGS
- F1 (cache-key wiring): RESOLVED.
  - test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts:399 checks the read side: a seeded full-key entry is served with list===0. :409 checks the write side: the written key equals fullKey.
  - Both tests pass on pre-PR code, which is expected because there was no bug. Both go red under the two mutants #737 named (bare tree digest, constant versions), because either one makes the seeded entry a miss and the written key differ.
- F2 (self-alias dedupe): RESOLVED.
  - The guard is at src/adapters/quest.ts:1063 and the test at :427.
  - Dropping the guard makes `held` equal [item, item], which reads as task_reference_ambiguous, so the test goes red.
  - The case is legitimately reachable, not only through hand edits: quest's own resolver (quest-cli tasks.ts:1004-1015, QCLI-157) explicitly allows a task's own id among its aliases.
- F4 (docblock placement): RESOLVED. questListCacheKey (:1116) now has only its own one-line doc, and questListCache's docblock (:1127) sits directly above questListCache (:1141). No test needed; it is cosmetic.
- F5 (case folding): RESOLVED for the rollup path. See should-fix 1 for lore's other path.
  - referenceKey (:1023) is NFC followed by a per-code-point override, falling back to `.toLowerCase()`. That matches quest's aliasKey `caseFold(alias.normalize("NFC"))` (quest-cli records.ts:90-93) and findTask (tasks.ts:1397-1412) in both match and ambiguity.
  - Folding per code point also sidesteps toLowerCase's Final_Sigma context rule, which is correct.
  - Red under the pre-PR `toLowerCase`: NFC/NFD :444, STRASSE/straße :455, final sigma :465, fold-equal ambiguity :477.
  - The table pin (:489) and the every-entry test (:497) are red on pre-PR code only as import failures.
  - Pair timing: case folding is not new in quest. unicode-case-folding / caseFold appear in quest's phase-1 records (QCLI-19, QCLI-25, QCLI-156, and its ADRs). So this change brings lore toward the paired quest; it does not regress parity against an older one.
- F7 (malformed aliases): RESOLVED. The new semantics barely matter for a real quest. See nit 2.
  - Red pre-PR: the string-alias match giving drift (:518) and the non-string miss giving drift, named and capped (:561).
  - Guards that pass pre-PR: the irrelevant string alias with a miss giving not_found (:531), both halves of the mixed-array test (:543), and the null test (:553).

WRITER'S DISCLOSURE (U+1FBE, U+1FD3, U+1FE3): TRUE.
- All three are canonical singletons, and NFC maps them to U+03B9, U+0390 and U+03B0 before the table is consulted. referenceKey normalizes at :1025, and quest normalizes before calling caseFold too.
- So neither lore's table nor quest's FOLDING_MAP is ever consulted for them. Folding U+0390 and U+03B0 goes through their own table rows, which give the same output.
- There was no behavioural divergence. The rows are harmless parity rather than dead weight worth removing: they keep the generator's `--ts` set check exact, and deleting them would make it report MISSING.
- The U+1FBE test (:509-516) is not vacuous: its literal really is U+1FBE.

GENERATOR (scripts/gen-case-fold-table.mjs)
- It does regenerate the shipped table as a set (via `--ts`). It emits entries in ascending code-point order, which matches the committed order, so the sha pin should reproduce under the same runtime.
- Its design is sound:
  - It parses FOLDING_MAP as JSON and never executes library code.
  - Code points missing from the map fold to themselves, which is what makes the Cherokee identity overrides correct. I confirmed Cherokee uppercase U+13A0..13F5 is not a key in 1.1.1, while AB70→13A0 is.
- "From a pinned Unicode source, deterministically" holds only partly. See should-fix 2.

FINDINGS

Blocking: none.

Should-fix 1: src/commands/link.ts:884-885, outside the diff. lore's two read paths now disagree on non-ASCII references.
- Defect: verifiedViewTask still compares `detail.id` and the aliases with `.toLowerCase()`. It guards every per-task read: `lore tasks`, `lore link`, `lore orphans`, and the resolveTaskDetails fallback.
- Failure scenario: a task's id or alias is `straße`.
